findings.evidence: Crop 04: a detached dark short mark lies above the low first-e area immediately left of the tall loop. It has a thick left lobe and a smaller right lobe, so the accent direction cannot be securely read. The detached mark is preserved in the alternatives.

notes.text: The opening introduces a tree Gamma=(S,A,R), naming S, A and R in that order. The author writes A with a clean hooked right arrow to a decorated P_2(S), followed by the S-to-P(A) expression whose left-end arrow decoration remains uncertain. The subsequent source words call it an application and refer to injectivity and the two-vertex one-edge graph. These words influenced attention to the map sign but did not settle its crowded strokes.

Two indexed families (U_s) and (E_a) are introduced, followed by the displayed coproduct expression for X. The one-edge graph is represented by two filled dots and a single solid connector without arrowheads.

The author refers to the two components of Gamma “coupé en a_0”, then writes a binary decomposition X=X prime union X double prime. The definitions of the two parts occupy successive display rows, followed by avec and the displayed intersection E_{a_0}. The final coproduct index is visibly open like c, while the summand retains the a subscript. Both observed forms are retained with the stated uncertainty.

The paragraph uses the author’s quotation marks around “propre”, two occurrences of sss, and two inequalities. The lower character in the first inequality has a b-like stem, despite the earlier and neighbouring zero forms. The page ends with a parenthesized ambiguous label and the author’s sentence about a sommet-bout and U_s. This is a source description; no proof of the stated criterion was checked.

No date, title, explicit author question, or author proof-check annotation is visible on this sheet. The light pencil 27 in the lower left is retained as archive numbering, without a manuscript-page macro. The doubts retained in this return belong to the reading, not to explicit question marks by the author.

Mathematical cues considered during reading were the repeated family indices, the first a_0 and the neighbouring E_{a_0}, and the prose application/injectivity wording. These cues were not used to change contradictory visible strokes. The editorial H note about A prime and A double prime has no visible manuscript counterpart and is excluded from the page transcription.

workflow_feedback: The whole image was viewed once for layout, then each supplied half once and read line by line against both witnesses. Seventeen tight crops cover only remaining genuinely unsettled loci; related marks within one local passage share a single crop. Every crop was viewed once, with no repeat crop and no whole-half enlargement. The original source is 1692 x 2362; half b starts at whole-image y=1101. Bounds were checked before cropping; every focal mark is fully included, and no accidental clipped focal edge was observed. No OCR, external research, other pages, other readers, compilation, or proof checks were used. All 24 supplied C doubt IDs have retained/resolved findings. Resolving a C primary reading leaves against_C false; changed primary readings are flagged separately by against_C true. A final structural check verified required fields, allowed inventory values, all 24 doubt IDs, existing file references, and whole-image coordinate bounds; it was not a mathematical proof check.
